summary.title: How to be successful at Amazon (or any other large company for that matter)
summary.one_liner: A first-person Reddit post giving an ex-Amazon engineer's advice on mentors, documentation, project selection, and performance-review politics for getting ahead at large companies.
keywords: avoid being loaned to other teams
how to get promoted as an engineer
takeaways: Find a mentor outside your immediate team who is a few management levels up, plus an on-boarding mentor on your own team for day-to-day questions.
Management values predictability and on-time delivery; start with small tasks and document every project's goals, decisions, test plan, operations and results.
Choose projects with senior engineers involved and avoid ops-heavy, loaned-out, or trivial front-end/config work, since these hurt visibility and reviews.
Biannual OLR reviews drive outcomes; aim for Exceeds or better and avoid repeated mediocre ratings.
Protect your reputation, avoid repeating mistakes, and stay skeptical of management, treating the job as a business transaction.
summary.summary: The post is an informal, opinionated list of tips from a former Amazon engineer on advancing at large companies, and the author repeatedly warns readers to take it with a grain of salt. It is organized into a "What to do" section (mentorship, starting small, tracking KPIs, writing good code, documentation) and a "Don'ts" section (avoiding negativity, repeated mistakes, and trusting management blindly). It also discusses project selection, Amazon's semi-annual OLR rating process, and the technology stack and manager technical depth at Amazon. It is anecdotal rather than data-backed, and some advice is specific to Amazon's internal culture.
